newsitem.title: USA: Helms asks recall of U.S. ambassador to Vatican.
newsitem.headline: Helms asks recall of U.S. ambassador to Vatican.

text.p: Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chairman Jesse Helms urged on Friday that U.S. Ambassador to the Vatican Raymond Flynn be replaced because of alleged ethical violations.

Helms, in a letter to Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, said a report last December by the State Department's Inspector General raised serious questions about Flynn, who was mayor of Boston before becoming ambassador.

"The inspector general brought to light evidence that Ambassador Flynn had made improper and/or questionable charges against campaign funds while serving at the Vatican in clear violation of his ethics undertaking letter to the State Department's deputy legal adviser dated June 7, 1993," Helms wrote.

In the ethics letter, written before Flynn was confirmed as ambassador to the Vatican, Flynn said he would continue to maintain a campaign committee but that it would not spend any funds for political activity while he was ambassador.

But Helms said records compiled by the inspector general indicated that Flynn made credit card charges against his campaign fund for official travel and other expenses, which he later reimbursed, and wrote checks against the campaign committee account for apparent political activity.

"In light of these allegations -- in addition to his previous violations of State Department rules -- I hope that you will ask the president to recall Ambassador Flynn and appoint a new nominee to be ambassador to the Vatican," Helms wrote Albright.

Flynn has been reprimanded twice while ambassador. Once, for correspondence the State Department deemed inappropriate partisan criticism of Republican domestic priorities and again for using his campaign-account dollars for political purposes and diplomatic expenses and for having an embassy aide attend to family finances.
Flynn, like other ambassadors, received a letter earlier this month informing him that his term would expire in mid-July.
Flynn's mayoral campaign finances were the subject of a probe that resulted in two of his aides being sentenced to prison while he served in Rome.
